slot.brief: Given the solubility of a sparingly soluble salt of type AB2, compute Ksp including the common-ion-free stoichiometric exponents.

stem: A sparingly soluble salt $\text{AB}_2$ dissociates as $\text{AB}_2(s)\rightleftharpoons\text{A}^{2+}+2\text{B}^-$. If its molar solubility in pure water is $1.0\times10^{-2}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$, what is its $K_{sp}$?

verdicts.working: Let the molar solubility be s = 1.0×10⁻² M. Then [A²⁺] = s and [B⁻] = 2s, so Ksp = s(2s)² = 4s³ = 4.0×10⁻⁶.

working:
$[\text{A}^{2+}]=s,\quad[\text{B}^-]=2s$
$K_{sp}=s(2s)^2=4s^3=4(1.0\times10^{-2})^3=4.0\times10^{-6}$

Independent check: Let the molar solubility be s = 1.0×10⁻² M. Then [A²⁺] = s and [B⁻] = 2s, so Ksp = s(2s)² = 4s³ = 4.0×10⁻⁶.
